content.text: {"screening_id":"SCR_000096","question_assessments":[{"domain_id":"D1","question_id":"1.1","agent_response":"Y","evidence_location":"Methods—Participants, Data Handling, and Statistical Analysis (pp. 659–660); Table 1 (p. 663); Discussion—limitations (p. 664)","evidence_summary":"SGLT2i exposure was determined by clinical prescribing rather than random allocation. Before weighting, exposed patients differed substantially in left ventricular function, loop-diuretic use, renin–angiotensin-system inhibitor use, surgery type, non-elective surgery, and other prognostic characteristics.","rationale":"Clinical indication, comorbidity severity, kidney function, and clinician prescribing decisions can affect both SGLT2i exposure and postoperative AKI risk, creating clear potential for confounding.","agent_confidence":"High"},{"domain_id":"D1","question_id":"1.2","agent_response":"N","evidence_location":"Methods—Data Handling and Statistical Analysis (pp. 659–660)","evidence_summary":"Participants were classified once according to preoperative SGLT2i prescription status; the primary analysis did not split follow-up according to changes in treatment received.","rationale":"The analysis compared baseline exposure groups over a fixed postoperative seven-day window rather than dividing person-time by treatment received during follow-up.","agent_confidence":"High"},{"domain_id":"D1","question_id":"1.3","agent_response":"PN","evidence_location":"Methods—Data Handling (pp. 659–660); Table 1 (p. 663); Discussion—limitations (p. 664)","evidence_summary":"Many baseline variables were obtained from electronic medical records, including kidney function, ventricular function, comorbidities, medications, and surgery characteristics. However, exposure duration and adherence could not be established, and information on factors such as diabetes control, frailty, albuminuria, prescribing preference, and calendar-time changes was not reported.","rationale":"Several important variables were objectively recorded, but not all plausible baseline confounding domains were measured or characterized sufficiently, particularly factors influencing SGLT2i prescribing and AKI risk.","agent_confidence":"Moderate"},{"domain_id":"D1","question_id":"1.4","agent_response":"N","evidence_location":"Methods—Statistical Analysis (p. 660); Results (p. 661); Table 1 (p. 663); Discussion—limitations (p. 664)","evidence_summary":"Overlap weighting used a propensity model selected through Lasso and literature-based outcome associations. The model included ventricular function, hypertension, COPD, BMI, haemoglobin, creatinine, selected medications, surgery type, and a renal-replacement risk index. Important factors were not necessarily included, and coronaropathy remained imbalanced after weighting with an SMD of 0.179.","rationale":"Although the selected model balanced included covariates, the data-driven selection strategy and residual imbalance did not adequately address all important measured and unmeasured confounding domains.","agent_confidence":"High"},{"domain_id":"D1","question_id":"1.5","agent_response":"Y","evidence_location":"Methods—Statistical Analysis (p. 660); Results—propensity-score model description (p. 661)","evidence_summary":"The propensity-score model was based on preoperative variables. Intraoperative and postoperative variables such as vasopressor use, bypass duration, and postoperative support were not included in the reported adjustment model.","rationale":"The primary adjustment appears to have avoided controlling for post-exposure mediators or consequences of treatment.","agent_confidence":"High"},{"domain_id":"D2","question_id":"2.1","agent_response":"PY","evidence_location":"Methods—Participants (p. 659); Figure 1 (p. 661)","evidence_summary":"Eligibility required an indication for long-term SGLT2i treatment and excluded preoperative AKI, severe kidney dysfunction, and death before postoperative day 1. Eight patients who died before day 1 and 88 with preoperative AKI were excluded.","rationale":"Some selection criteria were related to determinants of both exposure and postoperative AKI risk. Exclusion based on survival to postoperative day 1 may also condition selection on an event occurring after exposure and surgery.","agent_confidence":"Moderate"},{"domain_id":"D2","question_id":"2.2","agent_response":"Y","evidence_location":"Methods—Participants and Data Handling (p. 659); Figure 1 (p. 661)","evidence_summary":"Long-term SGLT2i exposure existed before surgery, while final inclusion required survival until postoperative day 1 and absence of other exclusion criteria established at or near surgery.","rationale":"For previously treated patients, selection into the analyzed cohort occurred after initiation of the intervention, including application of a postoperative survival criterion.","agent_confidence":"High"},{"domain_id":"D2","question_id":"2.3","agent_response":"PY","evidence_location":"Methods—Participants (p. 659); Figure 1 (p. 661)","evidence_summary":"Patients dying before postoperative day 1 and patients with preoperative AKI were excluded after long-term exposure could already have occurred.","rationale":"Conditioning on postoperative survival and other factors related to treatment eligibility and renal risk could induce an exposure–outcome association, although the early-death exclusion affected only eight patients.","agent_confidence":"Moderate"},{"domain_id":"D2","question_id":"2.4","agent_response":"N","evidence_location":"Methods—Statistical Analysis (p. 660)","evidence_summary":"Overlap weighting addressed baseline confounding, but no inverse-probability-of-selection model, competing-risk correction, or other method specifically correcting selection into the cohort was reported.","rationale":"The propensity-score analysis does not by itself correct bias caused by eligibility or survival selection after intervention initiation.","agent_confidence":"High"},{"domain_id":"D3","question_id":"3.1","agent_response":"Y","evidence_location":"Methods—Data Handling (p. 659)","evidence_summary":"Exposure was defined as a preoperative SGLT2i medication appearing on prescriptions in the medical record; non-exposure was defined as no such medication. Discontinuation was separately defined as withdrawal at least three days before surgery.","rationale":"The operational definitions of exposed and unexposed groups were explicit and reproducible from the available records.","agent_confidence":"High"},{"domain_id":"D3","question_id":"3.2","agent_response":"N","evidence_location":"Methods—Data Handling (p. 659); Discussion (pp. 662, 664)","evidence_summary":"Exposure was retrospectively determined from preoperative prescriptions. The investigators could not determine when SGLT2i therapy began, its duration, or strict adherence.","rationale":"Intervention information was not documented by the study at treatment initiation, limiting accurate characterization of long-term exposure.","agent_confidence":"High"},{"domain_id":"D3","question_id":"3.3","agent_response":"N","evidence_location":"Methods—Data Handling (p. 659)","evidence_summary":"Exposure classification used prescriptions recorded before surgery, whereas AKI was measured during the subsequent seven postoperative days.","rationale":"Because the underlying prescription records preceded the outcome window, postoperative AKI or knowledge of it was unlikely to alter exposure classification.","agent_confidence":"High"},{"domain_id":"D4","question_id":"4.1","agent_response":"PN","evidence_location":"Methods—Data Handling (p. 659); Results and Table 2 (pp. 661, 664)","evidence_summary":"No specific institutional perioperative SGLT2i protocol was in place, and management was left to treating clinicians. The report does not identify systematic departures from ordinary clinical care caused by participation in this retrospective study.","rationale":"The retrospective observational design itself was unlikely to create deviations from usual care, although care practices were heterogeneous.","agent_confidence":"Moderate"},{"domain_id":"D4","question_id":"4.2","agent_response":"NI","evidence_location":"Table 2 (p. 664); Discussion—limitations (p. 664)","evidence_summary":"After weighting, differences remained in several intraoperative or postoperative care variables, including inotrope use, norepinephrine dose, bypass duration, and mechanical circulatory support, although most were not statistically significant. Detailed information on other nephrotoxic or kidney-protective co-interventions was not provided.","rationale":"The report does not provide enough information to establish whether all important co-interventions were balanced or appropriately handled; some reported differences may also be consequences of baseline severity or exposure.","agent_confidence":"Moderate"},{"domain_id":"D4","question_id":"4.3","agent_response":"NI","evidence_location":"Methods—Data Handling (p. 659); Results (p. 661); Discussion—limitations (pp. 662, 664)","evidence_summary":"Among 117 exposed patients, 65 did not discontinue treatment before surgery. The investigators could not assess strict adherence, duration of preoperative treatment, or postoperative reintroduction.","rationale":"There is insufficient information to determine whether the prescribed exposure was implemented and adhered to adequately for the intended causal contrast.","agent_confidence":"High"},{"domain_id":"D4","question_id":"4.4","agent_response":"PY","evidence_location":"Methods—Statistical Analysis (p. 660); Results (p. 661)","evidence_summary":"The primary analysis retained participants in baseline preoperative exposure groups and estimated a weighted causal relative risk using overlap propensity-score weights and sandwich variance estimation.","rationale":"This is generally appropriate for estimating the effect of baseline preoperative exposure as defined by the study, although uncertainty about adherence and heterogeneous discontinuation limits correspondence with a precisely specified target intervention.","agent_confidence":"Moderate"},{"domain_id":"D5","question_id":"5.1","agent_response":"NI","evidence_location":"Methods—Statistical Analysis (p. 660); Supplementary Figure 1 referenced in Results (p. 661)","evidence_summary":"The article states that postoperative creatinine values were missing, especially after transfer to surgical wards, but the main article does not report a clear participant-level proportion with complete AKI ascertainment over all seven days.","rationale":"It cannot be established from the supplied main report whether outcome data were available for all or nearly all analyzed participants.","agent_confidence":"High"},{"domain_id":"D5","question_id":"5.2","agent_response":"NI","evidence_location":"Figure 1 (p. 661)","evidence_summary":"The flow chart lists 15 patients with missing values before the final cohort was formed but does not specify whether intervention status was among the missing data.","rationale":"There is insufficient information to determine whether any participants were excluded specifically because SGLT2i exposure status was missing.","agent_confidence":"Moderate"},{"domain_id":"D5","question_id":"5.3","agent_response":"NI","evidence_location":"Methods—Statistical Analysis (p. 660); Figure 1 (p. 661)","evidence_summary":"Missing baseline values among retained participants were imputed using a random-forest algorithm, but the nature of the missing values for the 15 patients excluded in the flow chart is not specified.","rationale":"It is unclear whether those exclusions were caused by missing covariates required for the adjusted analysis.","agent_confidence":"Moderate"},{"domain_id":"D5","question_id":"5.4","agent_response":"Y","evidence_location":"Methods—Statistical Analysis (p. 660)","evidence_summary":"The authors explicitly regarded postoperative creatinine values as missing not at random, mainly because patients thought not to have renal failure were transferred to surgical wards.","rationale":"Availability of creatinine measurements depended on clinical status and therefore could depend on the participant's true AKI outcome. Different severity or lengths of stay between exposure groups could make this consequential.","agent_confidence":"High"},{"domain_id":"D5","question_id":"5.5","agent_response":"N","evidence_location":"Methods—Statistical Analysis (p. 660)","evidence_summary":"Postoperative creatinine values were excluded from the random-forest imputation and were not otherwise imputed or addressed with sensitivity analyses for informative missingness.","rationale":"No method adequately addressing the acknowledged missing-not-at-random postoperative outcome data was reported.","agent_confidence":"High"},{"domain_id":"D6","question_id":"6.1","agent_response":"PN","evidence_location":"Methods—Data Handling (pp. 659–660)","evidence_summary":"The primary outcome was based on objective serum-creatinine changes or initiation of renal replacement therapy using prespecified KDIGO thresholds.","rationale":"Serum creatinine itself is objective and unlikely to be directly influenced by knowledge of SGLT2i status, although testing frequency and renal-replacement decisions could be influenced by clinical knowledge.","agent_confidence":"Moderate"},{"domain_id":"D6","question_id":"6.2","agent_response":"Y","evidence_location":"Methods—Study Design and Data Handling (p. 659)","evidence_summary":"Data were retrospectively abstracted from routine medical files, and no blinding of clinicians or data extractors to recorded medication status was reported.","rationale":"Outcome assessors and treating clinicians likely had access to medication records and were therefore aware of exposure status.","agent_confidence":"Moderate"},{"domain_id":"D6","question_id":"6.3","agent_response":"Y","evidence_location":"Methods—Data Handling (pp. 659–660)","evidence_summary":"The same KDIGO creatinine and renal-replacement criteria and the same seven-day postoperative window were specified for exposed and unexposed participants.","rationale":"The formal outcome definition and data sources were comparable between groups.","agent_confidence":"High"},{"domain_id":"D6","question_id":"6.4","agent_response":"PY","evidence_location":"Methods—Statistical Analysis (p. 660); Table 2 (p. 664)","evidence_summary":"Creatinine monitoring became less complete after transfer to surgical wards. Exposed patients had a somewhat longer ICU stay and differed in baseline and postoperative severity, potentially providing more opportunity for laboratory detection of AKI.","rationale":"Although the biomarker threshold was objective, differential monitoring intensity related to exposure-associated severity and location of care could produce systematic ascertainment differences.","agent_confidence":"Moderate"},{"domain_id":"D7","question_id":"7.1","agent_response":"PN","evidence_location":"Introduction and Methods—Data Handling (pp. 659–660)","evidence_summary":"The authors identified stage 1 or higher AKI within seven days as the primary outcome and applied a defined KDIGO creatinine/renal-replacement algorithm. Urine-output criteria were not used, but no alternative primary measurement was reported.","rationale":"The reported measurement appears to follow the stated primary-outcome definition, though absence of a publicly available protocol prevents complete verification.","agent_confidence":"Moderate"},{"domain_id":"D7","question_id":"7.2","agent_response":"PY","evidence_location":"Methods—Statistical Analysis (p. 660); Results (p. 661)","evidence_summary":"The investigators considered unweighted analysis, inverse-probability weighting, and overlap weighting, and selected overlap weighting because inverse-probability weighting did not achieve optimal covariate balance. Covariates were selected through Lasso and literature-based screening.","rationale":"Multiple reasonable analytic specifications were available. The stated choice was based on balance rather than the observed treatment effect, but the retrospective, non-registered analysis retained meaningful analytic flexibility.","agent_confidence":"Moderate"},{"domain_id":"D7","question_id":"7.3","agent_response":"PN","evidence_location":"Methods—Statistical Analysis (p. 660); Results (p. 661); Tables 1–2 and Figure 3 (pp. 663–665)","evidence_summary":"The authors explained that overlap weighting was selected because it achieved better balance and reported unweighted outcome data as well as the weighted effect and confidence interval. No evidence is presented that the analysis was chosen because it produced a preferred AKI result.","rationale":"Despite lack of prospective registration, the reported reason for selecting the analysis was methodological and not apparently driven by statistical significance or effect direction.","agent_confidence":"Moderate"}],"domain_assessments":[{"domain_id":"D1","provisional_domain_judgement":"Serious","domain_rationale":"The non-random prescribing of SGLT2i created strong confounding by indication and disease severity. Although overlap weighting balanced included covariates, the model used data-driven covariate selection, left at least one important variable imbalanced, and could not address unmeasured factors such as prescribing preference, treatment duration, adherence, frailty, diabetes control, or calendar-time changes."},{"domain_id":"D2","provisional_domain_judgement":"Moderate","domain_rationale":"Selection occurred after long-term exposure initiation and included exclusion of patients dying before postoperative day 1 and those with preoperative AKI. These processes could condition on factors related to exposure and renal outcome, but the most concerning postoperative exclusion involved only eight deaths."},{"domain_id":"D3","provisional_domain_judgement":"Moderate","domain_rationale":"Exposure groups were explicitly defined from preoperative prescriptions and classification preceded the outcome. However, intervention start, duration, actual adherence, and some discontinuation information were not reliably established, allowing non-differential exposure misclassification."},{"domain_id":"D4","provisional_domain_judgement":"Moderate","domain_rationale":"Routine care was heterogeneous and no perioperative SGLT2i protocol existed. The baseline-group analysis was generally appropriate for the stated exposure contrast, but adherence, discontinuation, postoperative reintroduction, and balance of important co-interventions were insufficiently characterized."},{"domain_id":"D5","provisional_domain_judgement":"Serious","domain_rationale":"Postoperative creatinine data were acknowledged to be missing not at random because monitoring diminished after ward transfer. The extent of complete seven-day outcome ascertainment was unclear, and no imputation, weighting, or sensitivity analysis addressed informative missing outcome data."},{"domain_id":"D6","provisional_domain_judgement":"Moderate","domain_rationale":"The KDIGO creatinine-based definition was objective and formally identical between groups, but assessors were not blinded and monitoring intensity could vary with ICU duration, clinical severity, and ward transfer. This creates some risk of differential AKI ascertainment."},{"domain_id":"D7","provisional_domain_judgement":"Moderate","domain_rationale":"The primary AKI outcome was clearly identified, and the authors gave a methodological reason for using overlap weighting. Nevertheless, no prospective protocol or registration was reported, and multiple weighting and model-specification choices created analytic flexibility that cannot be fully evaluated."}],"agent_overall_provisional_judgement":"Serious","agent_overall_rationale":"The result has serious risk of bias, principally from residual confounding by indication and severity and from acknowledged informative missingness of postoperative creatinine measurements without an adequate corrective analysis. Additional moderate concerns arise from post-exposure selection, uncertain exposure adherence and duration, heterogeneous perioperative management, potentially differential outcome surveillance, and lack of prospective analytic specification. No domain was judged critical, but the serious concerns could materially alter the estimated association between preoperative SGLT2i exposure and AKI within seven days."}
